page: Amazon Web Services x8i.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, but offers a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in several areas. The processor features a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contribute to top-tier Geekbench multi-core scores of 22004.0 and Passmark CPU scores of 107115.33. Memory performance is strong, with cached read-only memory bandwidth reaching 7680.48 GB/sec. The server also demonstrates top-tier efficiency in Redis SET operations, processing 171.86 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 156.11 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the x8i.24xlarge offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, leveraging its massive 1.5 TB DDR5 RAM pool. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for disk-heavy operations. While CPU performance is strong, the absence of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it achieves top-tier prompt processing speeds for smaller LLM inference tasks using its AMX instruction set.

This server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput Redis deployments, memory-intensive data processing pipelines, and enterprise-grade software compilation. It is also well-suited for medium-scale LLM inference workloads that can leverage CPU-based matrix acceleration.
